```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D

DOC = "PCP-006"
UO = "viral_inactivation"
UO_TITLE = "Low-pH Viral Inactivation (Step 6)"

# --- doc-local derived scalars (pulled from the model; never typed) ------------------
uo = CFG.unit_op(UO)
ph = uo.param("ph")
hold = uo.param("hold_time")
temp = uo.param("temperature")
conc = uo.param("protein_conc")


def rng_of(p):
    return f"{p.prange[0]:g}–{p.prange[1]:g}"


def nor_of(p):
    return f"{p.nor[0]:g}–{p.nor[1]:g}"


def sp_of(p):
    return f"{p.setpoint:g}"


# Design STRUCTURE only — a protocol may state the planned runs, never a response.
scr_design = csv(f"doe_{UO}_screening.csv")
rsm_design = csv(f"doe_{UO}_rsm.csv")
n_scr, n_rsm = doe_runs(UO, "screening"), doe_runs(UO, "rsm")
c_scr, c_rsm = doe_centre_points(UO, "screening"), doe_centre_points(UO, "rsm")
n_scr_fact = int((scr_design.run_type == "factorial").sum())
n_rsm_fact = int((rsm_design.run_type == "factorial").sum())
n_rsm_axial = int((rsm_design.run_type == "axial").sum())

k_scr = len(D.screening_factors(UO))
k_rsm = len(D.rsm_factors(UO))
n_terms_scr = 1 + k_scr + k_scr * (k_scr - 1) // 2          # intercept + main + 2FI
n_terms_rsm = 1 + 2 * k_rsm + k_rsm * (k_rsm - 1) // 2      # + pure quadratics
df_res_rsm = n_rsm - n_terms_rsm
df_pe_scr, df_pe_rsm = c_scr - 1, c_rsm - 1
df_lof_rsm = df_res_rsm - df_pe_rsm

n_params = len(uo.parameters)
n_multi = sum(1 for p in uo.parameters if p.study == "multivariate")
n_uni = n_params - n_multi
n_resp = len(D.responses(UO))

# Acceptance criteria (criteria, not outcomes). acceptance_for back-calculates the STEP
# floor for a viral-clearance response and returns the DS specification for the others.
acc_xmulv = D.acceptance_for(UO, "xmulv_lrf")
cum_xmulv = float(cqa_reg[cqa_reg.key == "lrv_xmulv"].iloc[0].acc_low)
```

# Purpose and scope {#sec-purpose}

Low-pH viral inactivation is the dedicated inactivation step for enveloped virus in the
A-Mab drug substance process, and it is Step `{python} f"{uo.step:g}"` of the train. It
receives the Protein A eluate, which is already acidic, titrates it to the target pH,
holds it under mixing for a defined time at a controlled temperature, and neutralises it
for the cation exchange step that follows (Step 7). This plan defines the studies that
will characterize the step, and it fixes the acceptance and decision criteria before any
data are generated.

The plan covers the `{python} f"{n_params:g}"` process parameters of the low-pH hold and
the `{python} f"{n_resp:g}"` responses measured across them. Of those parameters,
`{python} f"{n_multi:g}"` enter a multivariate design and `{python} f"{n_uni:g}"` is
assessed one factor at a time, as assigned by the pre-characterization risk assessment
(RA-001). All studies are executed on a qualified
scale-down model (SDM) of the commercial hold vessel, and the clearance measurements use a
separate small-scale virus spiking model. The work supports the technology transfer
described in PTP-001, it forms part of the Stage 1 process design record expected under
the lifecycle approach [@fda2011], and the clearance element follows the viral safety
framework of ICH Q5A(R2) [@ichq5a].

Three things sit outside this plan. Confirmation of the ranges at commercial scale belongs
to Stage 2 and to the process performance qualification campaign (PPQ), not to
characterization.
The enveloped-virus clearance credited to anion exchange and to small-virus retentive
filtration is characterized under PCP-008 and PCP-009, so only the contribution of this
step is studied here. Host cell protein (HCP) precipitates during a low-pH hold and is
removed by the depth filtration that follows the neutralisation, but the extent of that
clearance is not predictable and no HCP claim will be made for this step [@amab2009].

# Objectives {#sec-objectives}

The characterization has five objectives, and each one supports a decision the control
strategy has to make.

- (i) Quantify the effect of inactivation pH, hold time and temperature on the
  inactivation of enveloped virus, measured as the XMuLV log reduction factor (LRF), over
  the ranges given in @sec-factors.
- (ii) Quantify the effect of the same three parameters on the two quality attributes the
  hold can change, which are aggregate content and acidic charge variants.
- (iii) Define the design space, which is the region inside the characterized space over
  which every response meets the criterion set for it in @sec-acceptance, and establish
  where the normal operating ranges sit inside it.
- (iv) Establish a proven acceptable range (PAR) for each multivariate parameter against
  each attribute the step governs, by the two analyses specified in @sec-par. The
  acceptable range of A-Mab concentration follows from the univariate assessment
  (@sec-univariate) against the same criteria.
- (v) Provide the evidence needed to classify every parameter under SOP-4001 and to state
  the contribution of the step to the control strategy.

Objectives (i) and (iii) carry the viral safety claim, which is the reason the step is
characterized at all, and the remaining objectives bound the conditions under which that
claim holds and turn it into something the control strategy can act on. Every objective is
answered in PCR-006, which is the deliverable of this plan.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior}

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge

The step inactivates enveloped virus by acid denaturation. Exposure to low pH changes the
conformation of the viral envelope glycoproteins irreversibly, so the particle can no
longer fuse with a host cell membrane, and the loss of infectivity follows first-order
kinetics in the duration of the exposure [@ichq5a]. The rate constant rises as pH falls
and as temperature rises, and the same two conditions act on the antibody, which is only
marginally stable at low pH, so the step is a balance between the inactivation the process
needs and the aggregation it has to avoid [@amab2009].

Novacyte Biologics has operated a low-pH hold on three prior humanized IgG1 products
(X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab), and the conditions of the hold have not changed materially
across those products or through A-Mab clinical supply. The inactivation kinetics
established on the prior products transfer directly to A-Mab, so the kinetic form of the
step is settled platform knowledge before the first run is executed. Prior knowledge of
that kind is what allows a characterization study to confirm and bound a known mechanism
instead of establishing one.

Three expectations follow from the mechanism, and the study is designed to confirm or
refute each of them. Inactivation should improve as pH falls and worsen as pH rises, so
the high edge of the pH range is the direction of risk for viral safety. Aggregate content
should rise with hold time and with temperature, because acid-induced partial unfolding is
slow and thermally activated, which makes the long and warm corner of the design the
direction of risk for product quality. Acidic charge variants should increase over the
hold through deamidation of asparagine residues, and the increase is expected to be small
against the width of the drug substance criterion.

The characterization ranges are wider than the ranges the commercial process will use, and
each edge has a reason taken from the platform studies [@amab2009]. Inactivation pH is
studied over `{python} rng_of(ph)` against a normal operating range (NOR) of
`{python} nor_of(ph)`. Earlier univariate work on the platform found that antibody
precipitation can occur just below the low edge of that range, so it was not extended
further. The high edge is the highest pH at which inactivation has been studied on the
platform, and it lies well above the normal operating range, so that loss of inactivation
at high pH is bounded inside the design. Hold time is studied over `{python} rng_of(hold)`
`{python} hold.unit`, which reaches well past the upper edge of its normal operating range.
Its high edge is the longest hold the platform has carried without loss of acceptable
product quality, and it leaves room for a hold extended by a downstream delay to fall
inside the characterized space. Temperature is studied over `{python} rng_of(temp)`
`{python} temp.unit`. The high edge sits above the normal operating range to confirm that
the antibody is stable there, since a warmer hold raises the rate of aggregation as well as
the rate of inactivation. The low edge sits below the normal operating range to measure how
much a colder hold slows the inactivation, which is the direction that carries the viral
safety risk.

## Quality attributes in scope {#sec-cqas}

The step sets one critical quality attribute (CQA) and can change two others. They are
given in @tbl-cqas with the acceptance criterion and the criticality of each. Criticality
follows the continuum approach of ICH Q9 [@ichq9]. It is assessed on two dimensions, which
are the potential impact of the attribute on safety and efficacy and the uncertainty
attached to that impact, and an attribute at the top of the scale (high or very high) is
treated as critical [@amab2009]. The Tool #1 score in @tbl-cqas is the product of the two
dimensions, so it does not rank the three attributes in the order their criticality does.
An attribute of very high impact whose behaviour is well established scores below one of
moderate impact that is less well characterized.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(["lrv_xmulv", "aggregates_hmw", "acidic_variants"]))
print()
print(": Quality attributes governed by the low-pH hold. {#tbl-cqas}")
```

Enveloped-virus clearance is the attribute the step exists to deliver and it carries the
highest criticality of the three. Its Tool #1 score is the middle one, because the
consequence of a failure is severe but the mechanism is well understood and little
uncertainty attaches to it. Aggregate content carries the highest score of the three,
because its impact is the one assessed with the most uncertainty.

The acceptance criterion for enveloped-virus clearance is cumulative over the
process, so no single step meets it alone. A-Mab claims enveloped-virus clearance at three
steps, which are the low-pH hold, anion exchange (Step 8) and small-virus retentive
filtration (Step 9), and the three mechanisms are independent of one another. The
contribution required from this step follows from the cumulative requirement and from the
clearance credited to the other two, and it is stated in @sec-acceptance.

Aggregate content is formed in the production bioreactor and reduced at cation exchange
(PCP-003 and PCP-007). This step neither forms it in culture nor clears it, but it can add
to it, and the study is designed to bound how much it adds across the characterized space.
Acidic charge variants are of very low criticality and have a wide criterion, and they are
measured here because deamidation is dependent on pH and on time, and because this hold is
the longest low-pH exposure in the purification train.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters {#sec-risk}

RA-001 assigned a study type to every parameter of this step before this plan was written.
It scored each parameter on the severity of the attribute the parameter puts at risk, on
how often a departure was expected to occur before the step was characterized, and on how
likely such a departure was to be detected in process, and it combined the three into an
initial risk priority number. The study type followed from whether the parameter was
carried into the designed experiment for the step. Every parameter that acts on
enveloped-virus clearance ranks at the top of that assessment, because the attribute is
scored at the highest severity in the register and cannot be measured on a routine
manufacturing batch.

Three parameters carried a multivariate assignment. Inactivation pH, hold time and
temperature all enter the inactivation rate, they act on the product at the same time, and
there is no prior basis for assuming that their effects stay additive across the full
width of the characterization ranges. A design that varied them one at a time could
neither detect that nor bound it.

A-Mab concentration carried a univariate assignment. RA-001 scored it against process
performance rather than against a quality attribute of the step, which put it lowest of
the four parameters, and it is not a factor of the designed experiment. Its normal
operating range is the whole of its characterization range, because the concentration of
the Protein A eluate is set upstream (PCP-005) and is not adjusted at this step.

Other operating variables of the step are fixed procedurally by the operation SOP
(SOP-2009) and were not carried forward as characterization parameters. They include the
identity and molarity of the titrant, the neutralisation target, the mixing configuration
and the vessel material. Their control is verified in the batch record for each run, and a
departure from any of them is handled as a deviation.

# Materials and methods {#sec-methods}

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

The studies are executed on a scale-down model of the commercial hold vessel, qualified
under SOP-1001 before the first characterization run. A hold has no separation mechanism,
so the model carries fewer scaling dependencies than a chromatography step, and the
scale-independent variables (pH, temperature, hold time, protein concentration) can simply
be operated at their commercial equivalents. The scale-dependent variables are vessel
geometry, mixing time, titration rate and the ratio of surface area to volume, and they
are set so that the titration and neutralisation profiles match the commercial records.

Qualification compares replicate runs at the set-point against the commercial-scale record
for the same operation. The comparison covers the attributes of the load, the attributes
of the pool at the end of the hold, and the time taken to reach the target pH on
titration. The last of these matters more here than it would at a chromatography step,
because the hold clock starts when the target pH is confirmed and any difference in
titration time is a difference in exposure. The number of replicate runs, and the
difference judged acceptable for each compared attribute, are fixed in the qualification
protocol issued under SOP-1001 before the comparison is run. The acceptance criterion for
qualification is given in @sec-acceptance.

Virus clearance is measured on a separate small-scale spiking model, which is what a
clearance claim requires [@ichq5a]. Live XMuLV is added to the load at a defined titre,
and the spiked volume is held to a small fraction of the load volume so that the matrix of
the material is not altered. Spiked material is handled in a laboratory that is physically
separate from manufacturing and none of it returns to the process. The load for the
spiking runs is Protein A eluate from a representative campaign, so that the properties
that could change the outcome (buffer composition, protein concentration, impurity burden)
are those the commercial step will see.

Centre-point replicates carry the pure-error term for the lack-of-fit tests described in
@sec-stats. The screening design includes `{python} f"{c_scr:g}"` centre points and the
response-surface design includes `{python} f"{c_rsm:g}"`, which give
`{python} f"{df_pe_scr:g}"` and `{python} f"{df_pe_rsm:g}"` degrees of freedom for pure
error. Replication at the centre also gives the reproducibility of each response under
nominally identical conditions, which PCR-006 reports as a coefficient of variation per
response.

## Operation {#sec-operation}

The step is operated as a batch hold in three phases. The Protein A eluate is titrated to
the target pH with acid under mixing, and the pH is measured in the vessel after a defined
mixing period. The batch is then held for the target time with the jacket controlling
temperature, and the hold clock starts when the target pH has been confirmed. At the end
of the hold the batch is neutralised to the load condition of the cation exchange step and
filtered through a depth filter, which removes precipitated HCP and any product that came
out of solution during the hold.

Set-points and normal operating ranges for the four parameters are given in @tbl-params.
The buffers, the titrant and the neutralisation base are prepared and released to platform
specifications under SOP-2009. They are identity and quality controlled, and they are not
characterization parameters. The load is the Protein A eluate produced under PCP-005, and
its attributes (concentration, aggregate content, HCP burden) are controlled at that step.

## Analytical methods {#sec-assays}

Each response is measured by one validated method, and the three methods are given in
@tbl-sops. Enveloped-virus inactivation is measured as the XMuLV log reduction factor by
infectivity titration (AMV-3017), read at the 50 % tissue culture infectious dose
endpoint. The log reduction factor is the log₁₀ of the total virus in the spiked load
minus the log₁₀ of the total virus recovered at the end of the hold. Both terms are total
quantities, so the calculation accounts for the volume change on titration.

Aggregate content is measured by size exclusion chromatography (SEC-HPLC, AMV-3011) and
reported as the percentage of high molecular weight species. Acidic charge variants are
measured by imaged capillary isoelectric focusing (icIEF, AMV-3013) and reported as the
percentage area of the acidic region. Both are platform methods already validated for
A-Mab drug substance, so their performance is documented in the validation reports and is
not reproduced in this plan.

Two properties of the infectivity assay bound what the study can conclude. Its
intermediate precision is a standard deviation of
`{python} f"{amv_3017_precision:g}"` log₁₀, which sets the smallest difference in log
reduction factor the design can resolve and is the reason an effect is judged against the
pure-error term of the design. Its limit of quantitation is
`{python} f"{amv_3017_loq:g}"` log₁₀ TCID50/mL, which together with the achievable spike
titre sets the largest reduction the study can report. A condition that inactivates the
spike below the limit of quantitation is reported as a reduction of at least the
measurable value, and it is not extrapolated beyond it.

## Sampling plan {#sec-sampling}

Sampling is designed so that every run yields one infectivity result, one aggregate result
and one charge-variant result, and so that the centre points also give the shape of the
inactivation curve.

Each run is sampled at three points. The first sample is taken from the spiked load before
titration and fixes the starting virus titre. The second is taken at the end of the hold,
immediately before neutralisation, and carries the infectivity, aggregate and
charge-variant results for that run. The third is taken after neutralisation and depth
filtration and is retained as a reserve for investigation.

The centre-point runs are sampled during the hold as well, at
`{python} f"{hold.prange[0]:g}"` and `{python} sp_of(hold)` `{python} hold.unit`. These
samples confirm the shape of the inactivation curve without adding runs to the design, and
they carry the evidence for the first-order assumption that any statement about hold time
relies on. Product quality samples are not taken during the hold, because the aggregate
response of the step is defined at the end of it.

Every sample is assayed inside the stability period established for its method. Sample
identity, time of collection and storage condition are recorded in the batch record of the
run, and a sample whose record is incomplete is not used in the analysis.

## Statistical methods {#sec-stats}

All analysis follows the procedure for the design and analysis of designed experiments
(SOP-1002). Each factor is coded so that the centre of its characterization range is zero
and the two edges are −1 and +1, which puts the estimated effects on a common scale and
makes them comparable across factors measured in different units.

The screening analysis fits all main effects and all two-factor interactions by ordinary
least squares. An effect is reported as twice the coded coefficient, which is the change
in the response between the two edges of the range. Significance is judged at α = 0.05.
The screening model has `{python} f"{n_terms_scr:g}"` terms in
`{python} f"{n_scr:g}"` runs, so it is close to saturated. It is used to identify which
factors and which interactions are active, and it is not used as a predictive model.

The response-surface analysis fits the full quadratic model in the same factors, adding
the pure quadratic terms so that curvature can be estimated. That model is the predictive
model, and it is the basis of the design space declared in @sec-acceptance and of the
proven acceptable ranges derived in @sec-par. Its adequacy is judged on the overall F
test, on R², on the adjusted R², on the predicted R² computed from the predicted residual
error sum of squares (PRESS), and on an analysis of variance that partitions the residual
into lack of fit and pure error. With `{python} f"{n_rsm:g}"` runs and `{python} f"{n_terms_rsm:g}"` terms the
design leaves `{python} f"{df_res_rsm:g}"` residual degrees of freedom, of which
`{python} f"{df_pe_rsm:g}"` are pure error and `{python} f"{df_lof_rsm:g}"` are lack of
fit.

A factor with no significant effect on any response is not dropped from the record. It is
reported as inactive over the range studied, it is classified on that basis, and it stays
in the knowledge space as evidence that the responses are robust to it. A null result of
that kind is one of the more useful outcomes a characterization study can produce, because
it removes a parameter from the list of things the control strategy has to hold tightly.

Commercial-scale capability is estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches, with every parameter drawn inside its normal
operating range. Capability is reported as a one-sided Cpk against the governing limit,
because each criterion for this step binds in one direction only. Run order within each
design is randomised, and the randomisation is recorded before execution so that it cannot
be adjusted afterwards.

# Study design {#sec-design}

## Factors, ranges and study type {#sec-factors}

The design separates the three parameters that act on the inactivation rate from the one
that does not. @tbl-params gives the set-point, the characterization range, the normal
operating range and the study type for each of the four parameters.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(plan_params(UO))
print()
print(": Parameters, ranges and study type for the low-pH hold. {#tbl-params}")
```

The characterization ranges are the edges of the knowledge space and the normal operating
ranges are where the commercial process will run. Every characterization range covers the
whole of its normal operating range and extends past it in the direction in which an
excursion would carry risk, which is what makes these studies usable for assessing a
deviation later in the life cycle. A-Mab concentration is the exception in the table. Its
normal operating range is its whole characterization range, because the value is inherited
from the Protein A eluate (PCP-005) and is not adjusted at this step.

The three multivariate factors are coded A to C, and that coding is used in every effect
and coefficient table of PCR-006. The legend is given in @tbl-legend.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.factor_legend_df(UO))
print()
print(": Factor legend for the multivariate designs. {#tbl-legend}")
```

## Screening design {#sec-screening}

The screening study is a two-level full factorial in the three multivariate factors,
augmented with centre points. It has `{python} f"{n_scr_fact:g}"` factorial runs at the
corners of the characterized space and `{python} f"{c_scr:g}"` centre-point replicates,
`{python} f"{n_scr:g}"` runs in total. A full factorial estimates all three main effects
and all three two-factor interactions without aliasing, which a fractional design in three
factors could not do, and the run count is small enough that the fraction would save
little.

The centre points serve two purposes. They estimate pure error, and they test for
curvature, because a difference between the mean of the centre points and the mean of the
factorial points is evidence that a first-order model is not sufficient. Curvature is
expected at this step, since inactivation is exponential in time and pH acts on the rate
constant. The response-surface study is therefore planned outright, and it is not made
conditional on the outcome of the screening study.

The planned coded design matrix is given in Appendix A (@sec-appa).

## Response-surface design {#sec-rsm}

The response-surface study is a face-centred central composite design (CCD) in the same
three factors. It has `{python} f"{n_rsm_fact:g}"` factorial runs,
`{python} f"{n_rsm_axial:g}"` axial runs placed on the faces of the cube, and
`{python} f"{c_rsm:g}"` centre-point replicates, `{python} f"{n_rsm:g}"` runs in total.
Facing the axial points keeps every run inside the characterization ranges, which matters
here because neither edge of the pH range can be moved outward, for the reasons given in
@sec-prior. A design with axial points outside the cube would place runs below the
precipitation edge and above the highest pH at which inactivation has been studied.

All three factors go forward from the screening design into the response surface. This is
a design decision and not a result of the screening study, since the factor set is small
enough that dropping one would save few runs, and each of the three is expected to be
active on at least one response. If the screening study finds a factor inactive on every
response, the response-surface design is executed as planned and the factor is reported as
inactive on the evidence of both designs.

The planned coded design matrix is given in Appendix B (@sec-appb).

## Univariate assessment {#sec-univariate}

A-Mab concentration is assessed one factor at a time, at the low edge, the set-point and
the high edge of `{python} rng_of(conc)` `{python} conc.unit`, with pH, hold time and
temperature held at their set-points. Each condition is spiked and assayed as a full run,
so the univariate results are directly comparable with the centre points of the
multivariate designs. Spiking every condition is deliberate. A higher antibody
concentration has been reported to slow low-pH inactivation [@amab2009], so the assessment
has to carry the log reduction factor and not the product quality attributes alone. The
acceptable range of A-Mab concentration is established from this assessment, against the
criteria in @tbl-acc.

The reason for the univariate treatment is mechanistic, and it rests on two expectations
the study will test. The rate of inactivation at low pH is set by the three multivariate
factors (pH, temperature, duration of the exposure), and it is not expected to depend
materially on the concentration of the antibody in which the virus is suspended.
Aggregation is expected to depend on concentration, but through a mechanism that is not
expected to interact with the hold conditions over the range studied. If either
expectation is contradicted by the univariate results, the parameter is escalated to a
multivariate study and this plan is amended before that study is executed.

The other operating variables named in @sec-risk are not studied at all. They are held
procedurally and their control is verified in the batch record of each run.

# Acceptance and decision criteria {#sec-acceptance}

The study passes when three conditions hold together: the scale-down model is qualified,
every response model is adequate, and the design space defined from those models
contains the normal operating ranges of the parameters. Each of the three is defined below
before execution, and none of them may be redefined after the data are seen.

@tbl-acc gives the criterion each response has to meet and the basis of each criterion.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.acceptance_table(UO))
print()
print(": Acceptance criteria for the measured responses. {#tbl-acc}")
```

Two of the three criteria are drug substance specifications and apply to the pool as it
leaves the step. The third does not work that way. Enveloped-virus clearance is claimed
cumulatively over three steps, so the criterion for this step is the cumulative
requirement of `{python} f"{cum_xmulv:g}"` log₁₀ less the clearance credited to anion
exchange and to small-virus retentive filtration, which leaves
`{python} f"{acc_xmulv[0]:.2f}"` log₁₀ for the low-pH hold. That figure is a floor and not
a target. The step is expected to deliver more than the floor, and the margin above it is
what allows the cumulative claim to survive a weak result at one of the three contributing
steps.

The scale-down model is qualified when the difference between the two scales at every
compared attribute falls inside the difference set for that attribute in the qualification
protocol (@sec-sdm). The criterion is an equivalence criterion and not a test for a
significant difference, because a failure to find a difference over a small number of runs
is not evidence that the two scales agree. A model that fails on any attribute is corrected
and requalified, and characterization does not begin until it passes. The qualification
report is issued under SOP-1001 and is referenced by PCR-006.

A response model is adequate when the overall F test is significant at α = 0.05 and the
lack-of-fit test against pure error is not significant at the same level. The predicted R²
is reported alongside the adjusted R², and a large gap between the two is treated as
evidence of over-fitting even where the lack-of-fit test passes. No numerical threshold is
set for R² in this protocol, because no such threshold is grounded in prior data for this
step, and a value chosen for the occasion would carry no information. Where a model is
adequate but the fitted surface is flat against the precision of the assay (@sec-assays),
the parameter is reported as inactive over the range studied and not as a small effect.

The design space is declared as the set of conditions inside the characterized space
at which every response in @tbl-acc is predicted to meet its criterion. It is declared
from the response-surface models. The screening models identify which factors are active
and they are not used to draw the boundary. The study passes on this criterion when the
normal operating ranges of the three multivariate parameters lie inside the design space,
and when the worst-case corners of the normal operating box lie inside it as well. For viral
safety the worst case is the corner at the highest pH, the shortest hold and the lowest
temperature. For product quality it is the corner at the lowest pH, the longest hold and
the highest temperature. Both are evaluated explicitly and reported whether or not they
pass.

Parameter classification follows SOP-4001 and the criticality continuum of ICH Q9
[@ichq9]. A parameter whose variation across its normal operating range moves a critical
quality attribute measurably is a critical process parameter (CPP). It is classified as a
well-controlled critical process parameter (WC-CPP) where the control system holds it
comfortably inside the range that keeps the attribute within its criterion, and it is
classified as a CPP without that qualification where the range is narrow relative to the
control capability [@amab2009]. A parameter with no demonstrated effect on any attribute
is a general process parameter (GPP). The classification is an output of the study and it
is reported in PCR-006, so this plan states the decision rule and stops there.

Capability is reported for each attribute the step governs, as a one-sided Cpk from the
simulation described in @sec-stats. No minimum Cpk is set as an acceptance criterion in
this protocol. The capability figure is evidence about the margin the process holds at
commercial scale, and it is weighed against the criticality of the attribute when the
control strategy is defined in PCR-006 and consolidated in PCMR-001.

A failed criterion is not handled by widening the design space. If the design space does
not contain a normal operating range, the range is narrowed or the set-point is moved, and the
change is justified in PCR-006 against the same models. If a model is not adequate, the
affected design is repeated once the cause is understood, and a deviation is raised and
dispositioned before the repeat is executed. Any departure from this plan is recorded and
assessed for its effect on the conclusions, whether or not it changed a result.

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis) {#sec-par}

A proven acceptable range is a range of one parameter over which one quality attribute
stays inside its acceptance criterion. The design space is the multivariate region
described in @sec-acceptance. The two are different objects, and PCR-006 will report both,
because a univariate range is what a batch record and an operator can work with, while the
design space is what the filing claims. Both are drawn from the response-surface models,
which carry the multivariate parameters only. The acceptable range of A-Mab concentration
comes from the univariate assessment instead (@sec-univariate).

The acceptance basis is the same as in @tbl-acc. Aggregate content and acidic charge
variants are judged against the drug substance specification. The XMuLV LRF is judged
against the step floor back-calculated from the cumulative requirement, and it is never
judged against the cumulative figure itself, which no single step can meet.

Two analyses are run for each combination of multivariate parameter and governed attribute.
The first holds the other parameters at their set-points and scans the parameter of
interest across its characterization range. That scan uses the fitted response-surface
model on a grid of `{python} f"{D.PAR_CENTRE_GRID:g}"` points, and the proven acceptable
range is the contiguous part of the scan, containing the operating point, over which the
predicted response meets its criterion.

The second analysis propagates the normal operating ranges of the other parameters across
a grid of `{python} f"{D.PAR_GRID:g}"` points. At each grid point the other parameters are
drawn inside their normal operating ranges, the fitted model is evaluated, and model
residual variation is added, for `{python} f"{D.PAR_MC_N:,}"` draws per point. The proven acceptable range from this
analysis is the part of the scan over which the 95 % predictive interval of the response
stays inside the criterion. The whole interval has to clear the limit and not only the
predicted mean, so this analysis is a robustness criterion, it is expected to give the
narrower of the two ranges, and it is the one the control strategy uses.

Every proven acceptable range is reported as a two-panel figure, with the at-set-point
analysis on the left and the propagated analysis on the right. The parameter is on the
horizontal axis and the response on the vertical axis, the acceptance limit is drawn, the
acceptable part of the parameter range is shaded green, and the set-point and the normal
operating range are marked.

Where the two analyses agree across the whole characterization range, the entire studied
range of that parameter is proven acceptable and is robust to co-variation of the other
parameters inside their normal operating ranges. Where the propagated analysis is
narrower, PCR-006 names the attribute that binds and states the margin remaining between
the normal operating range and the edge of the proven acceptable range. Where the whole
characterization range is proven acceptable for every attribute, the binding constraint on
the design space is the multivariate corner and not any univariate range, and PCR-006
states that explicitly instead of leaving the reader to infer it.

Both analyses are bounded by the characterization ranges and by the fitted models. Neither
supports a claim about conditions outside the ranges studied. Neither replaces
confirmation at commercial scale, which belongs to Stage 2.

# Data management and integrity {#sec-data}

Study records are created, reviewed and retained under the ALCOA+ principles, so that each
record is attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, accurate, complete, consistent,
enduring and available.

Raw data are captured in the validated laboratory systems that serve each method. The
process conditions of each run are recorded in the electronic batch record of the
scale-down system, and the pH, temperature and time traces are retained as the primary
record of the hold. Infectivity results are transferred from the assay system into the
study data set under second-person verification, because a titration endpoint is read
rather than integrated.

The analysis data set is locked before any model is fitted and the lock is recorded. A
change after the lock is made as a new version with the reason recorded, and the analysis
is then repeated in full. Analysis scripts and their outputs are retained with the study
record, so that every table in PCR-006 can be regenerated from the raw data by a reviewer
who has only that record.

Access to the systems is role based. Audit trails are enabled and are reviewed as part of
the study record review, and records are retained for the period the licence application
requires.

with the clearance runs executed by the virology laboratory. Responsibilities are given in
@tbl-roles. Each function approves this plan before execution and reviews the report
against it.

|---|---|
| Process Development / MSAT | Owns this plan, qualifies the scale-down model, executes the process runs and authors PCR-006 |
| Virology laboratory | Executes the spiking runs, performs the infectivity assays and issues the clearance results |
| Analytical Development | Performs the size-variant and charge-variant testing and maintains the validated methods |

# Deliverables and schedule {#sec-deliverables}

The deliverable of this plan is PCR-006, the process characterization report for the
low-pH hold. The studies run in the four phases given in @tbl-phases, in that order. No
calendar dates are fixed here, because each phase begins only when the preceding one has
been reviewed and released.

| Phase | Activity | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scale-down model qualification against the commercial-scale record | Qualification report under SOP-1001 |
| 2 | Screening study, executed in randomised order | Screening data set and effect estimates |
| 3 | Response-surface study, executed in randomised order | Response-surface data set and fitted models |
| 4 | Univariate assessment, analysis, capability simulation and reporting | PCR-006, including the design space and the proven acceptable ranges |

: Study phases and their outputs. {#tbl-phases}

The report is issued into the characterization package and rolls up into PCMR-001. Where a
phase produces a result that changes the design of a later phase, the change is documented
before that phase begins.

# Risks and assumptions {#sec-risks}

Four risks could invalidate part of the study, and each has a defined response. They are
stated here so that the response is agreed before the risk materialises.

Titration at small scale reaches the target pH faster than at commercial scale, so a
commercial batch spends longer at intermediate pH before its hold clock starts. The
scale-down model would then understate the total acid exposure of the step, and with it
the aggregate burden. The response is to match the titration profile during qualification,
to record the time to target pH for every run, and to treat a run whose titration time
falls outside the qualified profile as a deviation.

The virus stock adds its own matrix to the load, and that matrix can interfere with the
infectivity assay or be cytotoxic at low dilution. The response is to hold the spike to a
small fraction of the load volume, and to run cytotoxicity and interference controls with
every assay, so that an apparent reduction caused by the assay is distinguishable from one
caused by the hold.

The study needs Protein A eluate that represents commercial material. If the eluate
available differs in concentration or in impurity burden, the aggregation responses will
shift and the fitted surfaces will describe the wrong load. The response is to record the
load attributes for every run and compare them against the release record of the eluate,
and to invalidate the affected runs where the load is not representative.

Inactivation may be complete at most design points, in which case the log reduction factor
is censored at the limit of quantitation and the models cannot estimate an effect from it.
The response is to maximise the spike titre within the constraint on spike volume, and to
treat a censored result as a bound rather than as a value in the analysis. The low-pH,
long-hold corner of the design is the one most likely to be censored.

Three assumptions underlie the plan. The SDM represents the commercial hold once it is
qualified under SOP-1001. The Protein A eluate used as load represents
commercial material. The clearance credited to the other two enveloped-virus steps in the
modular claim is achieved, and those two steps (PCP-008 and PCP-009) carry the evidence for
it. If the third assumption fails, the floor for this step rises and the design space
reported in PCR-006 is reassessed against the new floor.
